text:
maya: Quick alert — rolled int8 canary (horizon-liteq-v3) last night, seeing parse failure spike in structured funccalls this morning: ~4.7% vs ~0.2% baseline on fp32.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy horizon-liteq-v3 (10%) initiated by @maya at 2026-03-21T01:12:00Z

oncall-bot: Alert: parse_failure_rate( /invoke/horizon-liteq-v3 ) = 4.7% (threshold 1%)

maya: example bad output (trimmed):
```
{"tool":"create_issue","payload":{"title":"Order failed","user":42,},
}
```

alex: trailing comma + newline between object close and EOF. smells like token-level suffix noise or misaligned close tokens after K/V cache boundary.

sam: is this reproducible deterministically? can we run paired seeds (fp32 vs int8) over the failing set and diff token streams?

maya: kicked off paired parity run `parity/551234/2k` — should produce token diffs and alignment map.

katie: suggest immediate low-risk guardrail: enable soft-json-repair for canary only (strip trailing commas, close dangling brackets) + set max_retries=1 for parse failures. communicate to support.

devex: can do. also propose lowering per-model batch_window_ms to 10ms on canary so fewer interleaved kv-prefixes. flip will be scoped to canary tags.

alex: +1 on batch window. also plan a small schema-heavy eval: 300 prompts with nested arrays, code fences, and NDJSON lines. run on both fp32 and int8 and compute schema pass rate.

maya: parity results landed: int8 parse_fail 4.6%, fp32 0.3%. token-diff highlights extra " , " token emitted right after array close for int8 in ~70% of failures.

sam: share a diff snippet?

maya: pasted diff snippet:
```
FP32 tokens: ["{","\"actions\"",":","[","{","\"id\"",":","1","}","]","}"]
INT8 tokens: ["{","\"actions\"",":","[","{","\"id\"",":","1","}","]",",","\\n","}"]
```

katie: that aligns with a kv-cache boundary where int8 model emits an extra comma+newline before final brace. could be a subtle quantization-induced distribution shift.

alex: experiment plan:
- run with kv-cache disabled on int8 for a 1% traffic slice and measure drop in parse failures
- rerun tokenizer mapping probe (quant-aware token-split) to see if tokenization shift correlates
- run canary with postprocess-strict=false (i.e., allow soft repairs) vs strict to measure downstream error impact

devex: rolling soft-json-repair + retry-on-parse(1) + batch_window_ms=10 for canary now. will also enable postprocess-snapshot to s3 for each repaired output.

deploy-bot: Patch apply queued by @devex -> horizon-liteq-v3/canary (soft-json, retry=1, batch_window_ms=10)

maya: note: if repairs introduce incorrect args (i.e., hallucinated fields), we'll abort patch. set downstream_error abort threshold 0.25% for canary.

oncall-bot: Acknowledged. Will re-alert if parse_failure_rate > 6% or downstream_error > 0.25%.

sam: i'll run kv-cache-off replicate later today (job kv-off/551234) and post results here.

alex: i'll stand up the schema-eval harness and start the 300-prompt run; will report pass rates and token-alignment score.

katie: i'll draft a short blurb for support & product explaining temporary soft-repair behavior and how to recognize false positives. also add a note in the canary dashboard.

maya: FYI, observed failures skew to prompts with nested arrays + triple-backtick fenced codeblocks. maybe the model interpolates closing fences and trailing punctuation differently when quantized.

sam: action items
- sam: kv-cache-off replicate + results (today)
- alex: schema-eval 300 prompts (ETA 4h)
- devex: canary sanitizer roll and snapshotting (in progress)
- katie: support blurb + dashboard note (1h)
- maya: monitor metrics & abort if downstream_error > 0.25%

maya: TL;DR: int8 canary has suffix-token noise leading to trailing commas; mitigation = soft-json-repair + one retry + tighter batching; follow-ups = kv-cache toggle, tokenizer mapping probe, schema eval.

alex: I'll post token-alignment charts when done.

sam: will post kv-off numbers; if failure rate drops significantly, we know caching boundary interaction is main culprit.

katie: thanks team. keep any customer-facing reports minimal until we confirm no hallucinated args after repair. :eyes:

maya: closing loop for now. will update thread with metrics in 2h.
